relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a boy with LAD-I diagnosed by flow cytometry: "We report the case of an infant with LAD type 1"; no ITGB2 genetic testing or variant is reported, so the variants table is empty.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script in scratch, and every span was checked verbatim against the paper by script. No genetic testing is reported (diagnosis by flow cytometry of CD11/CD18), so no variant row was created; the person is in scope through the LAD-I diagnosis. n_patients_reported = 1 counts this LAD-I patient even though no ITGB2 variant is printed. first_author: the header prints 'Kartzow Rodrigo Vásquez-De' in surname-first order like the other authors, so 'Kartzow' was recorded; the true compound surname may be 'Vásquez-De Kartzow'. Age at diagnosis is not stated (diagnosis suspected during the admission at four months and confirmed later by flow cytometry at an unstated age), so it is 'not reported'. Age at last evaluation is the age at death ('at the age of four years'). Country 'Chile' is taken from the title and the hospital location, not from a stated ancestry. Possible contradiction: the otitis media is called 'non-purulent' (abstract and case history) but also 'suppurative' / 'mucoid suppurative'; both were recorded as observed features and the checklist item 'absence of pus formation' was left 'not reported'. Normal findings (D-27): urine and CSF cytochemistry normal, blood/urine/CSF cultures sterile, and CD4, CD8 and CD4/CD8 ratio normal were recorded as excluded abnormalities. The sentence on HIV ELISA, complement and immunoglobulins says only that the tests 'were done', and whether 'were all normal' covers them is ambiguous, so nothing was recorded for them. Normal CSF was not used to exclude the checklist item 'meningitis' (narrow finding vs broader item); 'significant weight loss' was not mapped to 'failure to thrive'. The bone marrow biopsy to rule out histiocytosis has no reported result. Discussion statements about LAD-1 patients in general (periodontitis, osteomyelitis) were not attributed to this patient. Table 1 is a literature-search count table and describes no individuals.
